summary: @vertexa/prisma-fetch-engine impersonates @prisma/fetch-engine and downloads native engine binaries from an unrelated personal GitHub fork
details: Package is published under the @vertexa scope but its package.json metadata mirrors the official Prisma package: name suffix prisma-fetch-engine, author Tim Suchanek <suchanek@prisma.io>, homepage www.prisma.io, repository github.com/prisma/prisma, and sibling dependencies @vertexa/prisma-debug, @vertexa/prisma-engines-version, @vertexa/prisma-get-platform that mirror the real @prisma/* scope. The bundled getDownloadUrl()/download() functions in dist/chunk-PEQQ7NRD.js construct Prisma engine binary download URLs against github.com/lh0x00/prisma/releases/download/engines-b436f5b358bf3b9d72861631111333dd40434f73/ — a personal fork owned by an unrelated GitHub user, not the prisma org. The fetched artifact is the Prisma Rust query/migration engine, a native binary that Prisma clients spawn as a subprocess, and no hash or signature verification is performed on the download. A consumer that installs this package believing it to be the official @prisma/fetch-engine and invokes its documented download() API will fetch and later execute attacker-controlled bytes as the Prisma engine binary, yielding code execution under the installer's Node process and host account.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
